parsedVerdict.reasoning: src/user/user.entity.ts is declared domain, but it is a TypeORM persistence model. It maps the class to a table and columns (@Entity('user'), @PrimaryGeneratedColumn, @Column with DB defaults, @JoinTable, @ManyToMany/@OneToMany relation mappings), which is persistence/infrastructure work. It also defines an ORM lifecycle hook, @BeforeInsert() hashPassword(), which calls argon2.hash at persistence time, coupling a save-time callback with an external crypto library (infrastructure concern). It also uses the class-validator @IsEmail() input-validation decorator, which belongs with DTOs at the application or presentation edge. Only the plain user data (id, username, email, bio, image, password and its links to articles) fits the domain role.

violations.message: Domain file carries persistence mapping: @Entity('user'), @PrimaryGeneratedColumn, @Column (with DB defaults), @ManyToMany/@JoinTable/@OneToMany define table schema and relations for TypeORM, which is an infrastructure (persistence) responsibility.

@BeforeInsert() hashPassword() is an ORM insert hook that calls argon2.hash. Hashing passwords on save is persistence/infrastructure work and belongs in an application service or infrastructure hasher, not the domain entity.
@IsEmail() (class-validator) on the email field is input validation, which belongs in DTOs (application/presentation), not in the domain model.
